title: Lease for an exactly-one role
description: Designed (docs/nodes.md 2.2), not implemented. The hub's grant of a role that at most one node may run at a time (today's only one: `feed-adapter`), sent to its holder in the state answer and renewed by every state post. The holder acts only on a grant it received in this process, never on one read from disk. Time is relative: the holder counts `ttl_s` from the moment it SENT the post this answer belongs to, on a clock that keeps running through suspend, and stops the role's work 15 s before that runs out. An absolute time alone is never a lease: clocks on the nodes drift and step.

role.description: The role this lease is for. One lease per role in the whole cluster. `feed-adapter` today; `training` later. A node ignores a lease for a role it does not know.

holder.description: The node id that holds it. A node acts only on a lease whose holder is its own id.

gen.description: The lease id: the pair [hub leader-lock generation, lease generation]. Always compared as a pair, the leader generation first, by numeric value: [3, 1] is newer than [2, 99]. The lease generation goes up by one each time the role moves to another holder; the leader generation each time another hub task takes the leader lock. Granting and renewing the same pair again changes nothing (a post may arrive twice). Where docs/nodes.md writes one number (`active (gen 14)`, `idempotent per (node, gen)`) it means this pair.

prefixItems.description: The hub's leader-lock generation when it granted or renewed this lease, a count.
The lease's own generation, a count.

ttl_s.description: How long the lease lasts, seconds, counted by the holder from the send of the post this answers. 90 in the design: longer than a hub handoff (35 to 60 s).

expires_at.description: Advisory only: the hub's own clock when the lease runs out, Unix seconds, for display and logs. A holder never decides anything from it.

counter.title: Counter
counter.description: A count that only goes up. A JSON integer from 0 to 2^53 - 1 (what every JSON reader keeps exact), or the same value as a string of decimal digits with no sign, no leading zero and no exponent (the only form allowed above 2^53 - 1; at most 20 digits). A reader compares the numeric values, never the strings and never as floating point.
